Channel 3 also shows large weights at a subset of cells, consistent with fixed target locations. Channel 2 is mostly small, suggesting a constant floor/empty channel. The output biases are all positive and slightly favour up/down over left/right, which fits a game where vertical pushing of objects is common. Reasoning: The combination of a 10×10 grid with an outer wall, an inner 8×8 playable area, five binary channels, and five actions (no-op, up, down, left, right) exactly matches the standard representation of Sokoban. The weights reveal fixed walls (channel 0), movable boxes and player (channels 1 and 4), and fixed targets (channel 3). Games like Snake, Pac-Man, or simple maze navigation do not fit: Snake has no fixed internal walls or targets; Pac-Man would have pellet/ghost channels with different spatial patterns; maze games lack boxes/targets. The presence of both movable object channels and fixed target/wall channels is characteristic of Sokoban.

Game: Sokoban (also known as Boxworld / Boxoban).

Description: The agent controls a player in a grid, moving up/down/left/right (or waiting) to push boxes onto target squares. Reward is given for each box placed on a target, and the episode ends when all boxes are on targets.
